They settle what a route is: the def element holds a definition that BDB sets in bold or in italics, and "Normally, each in a series of definitions will have a separate" element. They say a list of abbreviations will come with the lexicon's prefatory material, and they name no sign of punctuation. The printed book's list of abbreviations stands beside them in an annex copy, hebrewenglishlex00browuoft_djvu.txt, a scan's text whose printing the source does not name: it gives fr. as from, obj. as object, and the mark on a shortened Hebrew word, and it was searched for the others. So the geresh shape cites that list, and every other shape whose words say what a sign is for begins "unverified:". The route text names neither the entry nor the element it came from; the lane read both from the dictionary store's records/M5.jsonl by audit (builder/source-audit.mjs), which is evidence about the source and no part of any test. By the audit (axis: routes): 15,238 of 15,238 routes are the whole text of one def element, 755 of them with the store's cut flag, and none is a part of one. So this dictionary is the case of the ask's second sentence, where the store already gives each tagged definition its own route: a list inside one route offers no second reading that a test can tell from a second wording, so no comma divides at rest and the lists wait in branches.

Together 336 routes (axis: routes), 326 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row equals the route text on 336 of the routes. The source audit (builder/02-audit.mjs of v139, evidence about the source and no part of any test) covers the route store's rows: the source is the Open Scriptures HebrewLexicon's LexicalIndex.xml, and each of those 138 routes equals, exactly, the one definition element of an entry filed under the same letters, as the dictionary store's records of M33 show; all 339 records there hold one definition element each. So such a route comes from one field, and no test here stands on a guess about a field. The span store's records were not audited against the source's file here; their texts are of the same kinds as the route store's (a name, with or without a pointing word, a margin note or a bracket), and the span store's own fields were not read for any test. The source's own key is on file: its documentation at commit 21c9add13bc7 (<tabernacle>/corpus-lane-builds/moses-works-own-stamp-v1/strand-1-the-old-books/fetch/M5-openscriptures-HebrewLexicon-21c9add.pdf.txt, the section Lexical Index). That section names no hyphen.
